metaDescription: East Rochester sits in Columbiana County on the Utica flank. Learn how flank-position geology and old farm deeds shape your mineral interest's value.
heroLead: East Rochester is one of the smallest villages in Columbiana County, and small villages like this one are exactly where mineral interests tend to get lost across generations.
intro: East Rochester sits in southern Columbiana County, a village small enough that most of the surrounding land has stayed agricultural through the decades. As with much of Columbiana County, this area sits on the flank of the Utica/Point Pleasant play rather than in its structural core, so drilling activity has been light, and many mineral interests here have sat unleased and largely forgotten by the families who technically hold them.

sections.heading: Why forgotten minerals are common around East Rochester
paragraphs: In a small farming community like East Rochester, land often passes down within a family for generations with minimal formal review of what was reserved in the original deed. It's not unusual for current landowners to have no idea whether a great-grandparent severed the minerals decades ago, kept them intact with the surface, or sold them off separately at some point along the way.

sections.heading: What a title search actually clarifies
paragraphs: A search through the Columbiana County Recorder's office will trace every recorded conveyance affecting your parcel, showing whether a severance ever occurred and, if so, tracking the mineral interest forward to whoever currently holds it. That's the only reliable way to confirm ownership before deciding whether selling makes sense.

faqs.question: How do I even find out if my family owns minerals here?
faqs.answer: Start with a title search at the Columbiana County Recorder's office in Lisbon, tracing your deed back through prior owners to check for any severance or reservation of oil, gas or minerals.

faqs.question: Is East Rochester likely to see future drilling activity?
faqs.answer: It's hard to predict, since this part of the county sits on the flank of the play where development has historically been more selective than in core counties, but activity patterns can shift over time.

faqs.question: What if the original severance deed is over a hundred years old?
faqs.answer: Age alone doesn't invalidate a reservation. What matters is whether the interest has stayed active under Ohio law and whether the chain of title from that original deed to today is clear and unbroken.

faqs.question: What documents help establish my ownership fastest?
faqs.answer: Your deed, any lease or division order, and recent royalty statements if you receive them. Without those, expect a title search to be the first real step.

faqs.question: Could my family's interest already be at risk under the Dormant Mineral Act?
faqs.answer: If it's never been leased, never produced royalty, and never appeared in a recorded title transaction for 20 straight years, it could be vulnerable to an abandonment claim, so it's worth checking the county recorder's index for any pending notice.
